c: Heaven Sword throws a giant sword projectile at the closest enemy, which then starts spinning and boomerangs in the opposite direction it was thrown until it leaves the screen. Its
is doubled and damage more than doubles. It gains an extreme amount of knockback to push enemies back to compensate for the
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2.5x damage and have 10% chance to occur. This chance is affected by
- Heaven Sword's critical hit multiplier is doubled from 2.5x to 5x.
- Allows the Heaven Sword's projectiles to bounce off the edges of the screen twice. Upon bouncing, the sword completely reverses its horizontal and vertical speed instead of just one of them.
With Limit Break, Heaven Sword can be further leveled up.

Heaven Sword can deal critical damage by default. The more
the player has, the more likely they are to deal critical hits.

Heaven Sword travels much further when initially thrown than Cross, regularly being tossed offscreen only to come flying back. It is still the most effective when there are a lot of enemies, to ensure it pierces through as many enemies on the return trip as possible.

The automatic targeting nature of the weapon is both a blessing and a curse. While it removes the mental load of aiming, the closest enemy might not always be the enemy the player is trying to attack.
Its Speed is much greater than Cross, meaning that
PowerUp will amplify it greatly. This is not necessarily beneficial if the intent is to have these projectiles stay on screen as long as possible.
